title: Rigveda 3.28: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.28: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.28 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 207v-208r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.text: <sup>1</sup>AGNI who knowest all, accept our offering and the cake of meal, At dawn's libation, rich in prayer!

translation.original_ref: RV 3.28.2-6 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 31); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 208r
translation.original_text:
2pu̱ro̱ḻā a̍gne paca̱tas tubhya̍ṁ vā ghā̱ pari̍ṣkṛtaḥ | taṁ ju̍ṣasva yaviṣṭhya ||
3agne̍ vī̱hi pu̍ro̱ḻāśa̱m āhu̍taṁ ti̱roa̍hnyam | saha̍saḥ sū̱nur a̍sy adhva̱re hi̱taḥ ||
4mādhya̍ṁdine̱ sava̍ne jātavedaḥ puro̱ḻāśa̍m i̱ha ka̍ve juṣasva | agne̍ ya̱hvasya̱ tava̍ bhāga̱dheya̱ṁ na pra mi̍nanti vi̱dathe̍ṣu̱ dhīrā̍ḥ ||
5agne̍ tṛ̱tīye̱ sava̍ne̱ hi kāni̍ṣaḥ puro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ sahasaḥ sūna̱v āhu̍tam | athā̍ de̱veṣv a̍dhva̱raṁ vi̍pa̱nyayā̱ dhā ratna̍vantam a̱mṛte̍ṣu̱ jāgṛ̍vim ||
6agne̍ vṛdhā̱na āhu̍tim puro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ jātavedaḥ | ju̱ṣasva̍ ti̱roa̍hnyam ||
translation.text:
2Agni, the sacrificial cake hath been prepared and dressed for thee: Accept it, O Most Youthful God.
3Agni, enjoy the cake of meal and our oblation three days old: Thou, Son of Strength, art stablished at our sacrifice.
4Here at the midday sacrifice enjoy thou the sacrificial cake, wise, Jâtavedas! Agni, the sages in assemblies never minish the portion due to thee the Mighty.
5O Agni, at the third libation takewith joy the offered cake of sacrifice, thou, Son of Strength. Through skill in song bear to the Gods our sacrifice, watchful and fraught with riches, to Immortal God.
6O waxing Agni, knower, thou, of all, accept our gifts, the cake, And that prepared ere yesterday.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 208r (numbered 18r by the scribe) (OPenn image 209, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.28.2 ‹-pacataḥ tubhyam vā gha›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 208v (numbered 18v by the scribe), begins in RV 3.29.1 ‹-manthāma pūrva-thā›. Verses 3.28.2-6 end on this page; 3.28.2 begins on fol. 207v (numbered 17v by the scribe).
